chunks.body:
Joint venture with Signify continues to deliver robust revenue growth, backed by 
strong growth in indoor lighting portfolio, led by bats and down liters. While the lighting 
industry remains competitive, we continue to strengthen our position by leveraging our scale, 
engineering and designing capabilities and capitalize Signify's leadership position and long-
standing relationships with other customers across consumer and professional lighting 
categories. We expanded our baton production capacity to an industry-leading 5 million units 
per month, fully supported by backward integrated process. 
 
Pursuing an active product mix improvement strategy, we have launched 1,000-plus SKUs 
premiumizing the indoor lighting portfolio in the last two quarters and now we can cater to the 
entire portfolio of indoor lights. In the coming quarters, we are also focusing on expansion of 
range of outdoor lighting portfolio. We expect to start export deliveries to the largest retail 
chain in U.S. and Germany in Q2 and Q3 of this fiscal. 
 
Consumer electronics, LED TVs and refrigerators revenues for the quarter under review was 
INR987 crores with an operating profit of INR58 crores. LED TVs, the industry demand 
remained soft in value and mid-range segments impacted by sharp input cost inflation, majorly 
due to high memory prices on account of global supply tightness. 
 
However, demand for larger screen that is 50 and above and premium QLED/OLED 
televisions remained relatively healthy. We have initiated mini LED production and will 
transition to an OEM model by Q2 of '27, alongside launch of sound bar TV sets, expanding 

 
Dixon Technologies (India) Limited 
 
 
July 31, 2026 
 
Page 6 of 20 
 
our play in the premium home entertainment ecosystem. IFPD and digital signage business 
were also impacted due to increase in the memory prices in the quarter. 
 
Refrigerators. Q1 saw a huge uptick in commodity prices prompting industry-wide older 
inventory liquidation and slower fresh purchase and demand was further impacted by less 
intense summer and unseasonal rains. Despite these headwinds, we continue to see strong 
traction with healthy order book in direct cool and mini bars. Our ODM-led portfolio is scaling 
well, enabling higher value realization and faster refresh cycles.

prospects of the category supported by low household penetration, premiumization and 
increasing consumer demand. Rexxam Dixon Electronics, our 40-60 PCBA AC, PCB joint 
venture with Rexxam continues its strong growth trajectory, characterized excellent cash flow 
conversion and an industry-leading return on capital employed profile. 
 
Our new facility in Chennai will be operational starting August '26 with expanded capacity to 
meet the demand of our anchor customer. And we are in active discussion to onboard a couple 
of new customers for next year. 
 
Hearables and Wearables, a 50-50 JV with Imagine Marketing that is both continues to deliver 
strong financial performance, supported by broad-based revenue growth, healthy cash flow 
generation and a lean balance sheet. Building on this momentum, the JV is expanding into 
adjacent electronic categories, including dash cam, smart washes, power banks and mobile 
accessories. This diversification will improve capacity utilization and unlock operating 
leverage. 
 
With that, I'll conclude my remarks and both me and Saurabh are here to take -- are happy to 
take your questions. Thank you.

chunks.body:
Atul Lall: 
I would like to warmly welcome all our stakeholders to discuss our Q1 performance for '26-
'27. Key highlights for the quarter are as below. Revenues for the quarter ended June 30, 2026, 
was INR15,557 crores. EBITDA, excluding fair value gain on the stake held by Dixon Aditya 
Infotech Limited for the quarter was INR472 crores. PAT after minority interest and excluding 
fair value gain on the stake held by Dixon in Aditya Infotech for the quarter is INR218 crores. 
 
During the quarter 1 financial year '26-'27, the global and domestic electronics manufacturing 
landscape navigated a very complex macroeconomic environment, characterized by persistent 
inflationary pressure across commodities and supply chain. Sharp price spikes in core input 
components exerted temporary cost pressures across the broader hardware ecosystem. 
However, Dixon's agile cost-plus contract structures and pass-through mechanisms enabled us 
to deliver a strong revenue growth even amid temporary volume friction. 
 
Operating margin for the quarter reflected temporary compression on account of expiry of 
Mobile PLI 1 in March '26 and from increased selling prices driven by elevated input costs and 
broader supply chain inflationary factors. As increased input costs were passed through 
increase in selling prices, percentage margins look optically lower, mostly in mobile and IT 
hardware business. 
 
While the sunset of Mobile 1 incentives impacted short-term percentage profitability, Dixon's 
strategic pivot towards component backward integration, including display and camera 
modules, along with participation in mobile PLI 2 and ECMS positions the company to drive 
absolute profit growth and restore operating margins from the next fiscal of '27, '28. 
 
Washing machine and refrigerator business witnessed temporary margin pressures on account 
of volatility in polymer prices, other related input costs and adverse foreign exchange 

 
Dixon Technologies (India) Limited 
 
 
July 31, 2026 
 
Page 3 of 20 
 
movements. These impacts are expected to normalize with cost pass-through through measures 
and operational efficiencies taking effect. 
 
Operationally, our execution continues to be strong with the stable manufacturing efficiencies, 
disciplined cost management and sustained customer demand across key businesses. We 
remain focused on driving absolute value creation through scale, productivity improvements 
and deeper backward integration. As we continue to expand our capabilities and benefit from 
the new growth opportunities, including strategic partnerships and increasing localization, we 
remain confident to deliver sustainable long-term value for all stakeholders. 
 
Our strategic focus on balance sheet optimization and capital efficiencies continue to yield 
strong results, driven by operational leverage, high asset turns and potential capital allocation 
with return on capital employed and return on equity at 34.1% and 23.4%, respectively. 
Enhanced working capital discipline resulted in an optimal working capital cycle of negative 
five days. 
 
We remain firmly committed to drive value-accretive expansion across all verticals while 
maintaining strict capital management discipline and preserving superior return metrics for our 
shareholders. 
 
The timing of the announcement of the mobile phone manufacturing scheme is well aligned 
with the objective of the ECMS policy. While ECMS is focused on building a robust domestic 
component ecosystem, the mobile phone manufacturing scheme is expected to create sustained 
demand for critical components by driving higher mobile production and greater value 
addition. 
 
We expect the contours of the scheme to be announced in a couple of weeks and remain 
excited about the opportunities in mobile and IT hardware business. Now I'll share with you 
the business performance insights in each of the segments. Mobile and other EMS business. 
 
Revenue for the quarter for mobile and other EMS business was INR14,179 crores with 
operating profit of INR373 crores. During the quarter, mobile industry experienced a 
structured evolution from volume-led expansion to value-driven growth. While total shipment 
volumes saw a modest decline amid elevated global memory and component prices, the total 
industry market value expanded securely into the positive territory. 
 
Mobile volume performance was aligned with temporary demand contraction seen across the 
broader smartphone market by 10% to 12%, while our top line witnessed a strong revenue 
growth due to higher input cost realization. Our market position, customer engagement and 
manufacturing capabilities remain intact, and we expect 20% to 25% volume growth quarter-
on-quarter growth as consumer demand strengthens and we have a strong order book. 
 
We received the PN3 approval for our JV with Vivo in July '26, and we are now working 
towards the consummation of the transaction. We expect the JV to commence operations and 
start reflecting in our revenues from Q3 of the current fiscal. Construction of our 1 million 

 
Dixon Technologies (India) Limited 
 
 
July 31, 2026 
 
Page 4 of 20 
 
square feet facility in Noida with higher capacities for our anchor customer is almost 
completed.

KEI Industries Limited

Dear Shareholders,
During my years in this industry, I have seen India 
move from basic electrification to far more complex 
requirements across transmission, distribution, 
industrial applications and consumer wiring. The scale 
is now much larger. Government spending on roads, 
railways, metros, urban infrastructure and power 
networks is running alongside private investment 
in manufacturing, data centers, renewable energy, 
oil and gas, commercial real estate and housing. 
State industrialization programs are creating new 
manufacturing clusters, including in Uttar Pradesh 
and other high-growth regions. Each investment adds 
load to the power system and generates demand 
across EHV, HT, LT, control, instrumentation and 
housing wires.
The global operating environment remained uncertain 
during FY 2025-26. Tariff changes, geopolitical 
tensions, shipping disruptions and commodity-price 
volatility affected trade and supply chains. India 
continued to benefit from domestic demand, public 
capital expenditure and manufacturing investment. 
This base gives the wires and cables industry a 
broad demand pool. Renewable generation needs 
evacuation infrastructure. Data centers require 
incoming high-voltage power, medium-voltage 
distribution and copper cables within their facilities. 
Semiconductor and advanced manufacturing plants 
require stable power systems and cables built to exact 
technical standards. Transport and urban projects 
require large quantities of power, signaling, fire-
survival and specialized cables. This is the demand 
behind our investment plan.
Performance review
We closed FY 2025-26 with revenue of ` 11,748 crore, 
an increase of 20.66% over the previous year. EBITDA 
increased by 30.56% to ` 1,388 crore, while EBITDA 
margin improved to 11.81% from 10.92%. Profit after 
tax stood at ` 918 crore, with a PAT margin of 7.82%.
The wires and cables segment grew by 22.32% 
during the year. Higher copper and aluminum prices 
contributed to value growth, while our product mix, 
pricing discipline and operating controls supported 
the improvement in profitability.
Our order book reflects broad-based demand 
across EHV cables, domestic institutional business 
and exports, providing strong visibility across key 
markets and customer segments. This momentum is 
further reinforced by continued growth in our retail 
business, supported by a well-established dealer and 
distribution network and sustained demand across our 
market presence.
Demand across our core markets
Domestic institutional demand remained broad-based. 
Power transmission and distribution, solar and wind 
projects, thermal power generation, oil and gas, 
data centers, railways, metros, highways, tunnels, 
commercial construction and residential development 
continued to generate business. The semi-conductor 
and electronics manufacturing ecosystem is also 
creating demand for stable power infrastructure and 
technically reliable cable solutions.
Domestic institutional cable and wire sales stood at 
` 2,688 crore. Domestic institutional EHV cable sales 
increased by 82% to ` 559 crore. Our existing EHV 
facility operated close to full capacity, supported by 
established approvals, execution experience and 
customer relationships. We expect EHV demand to 
remain strong as India expands transmission capacity 
and strengthens the grid for rising power generation 
and consumption.
The dealer and distribution business delivered sales of 
` 6,349 crore, an increase of 25% and accounted for 
54% of overall sales. Our active dealer base reached 
approximately 2,125 at the end of the year. Housing 
wire sales also grew by approximately 32% during 
the year.
Our retail plan is focused on productivity and market 
quality. We are increasing the network selectively, 
strengthening capable dealers and replacing weaker 
partners where required. Eastern and southern 
India remain priority markets. We are adding sales 
personnel, onboarding dealers and increasing local 
market engagement in these regions. Product quality, 
availability, brand investment and service support will 
remain central to this expansion.
Exponential exports
Export sales increased by 45% to ` 1,833 crore 
during FY 2025-26. We now serve customers across 
more than 60 countries, with established business 
in the Middle East, Australia and Africa and a 
growing presence in Europe and the United States. 
Our export mix includes EHV, HT and LT cables

We delivered strong and broad-based financial performance during FY 2025-26. Net sales reached 
` 11,748 crore, marking a 20.66% y-o-y increase. EBITDA rose 30.56% to ` 1,388 crore with margins 
expanding to 11.81%. Profit after tax improved by 31.88% to ` 918 crore, driven by operating leverage, 
better working capital management and a disciplined shift to high-margin businesses. The revenue

used in utilities, renewable energy, oil and gas and

The United States market had slowed as tariff 
uncertainty affected customer decisions. With tariff-
related issues now easing, business conditions have 
improved and customer engagement has resumed. 
We are reconnecting with existing customers while 
pursuing new accounts, supported by strong demand 
visibility from the market. We therefore expect the 
US to contribute sizeable growth to our exports 
and remain an important growth market over the 
coming years.
We have also started building business in Europe, 
including opportunities linked to solar and other 
energy projects. Australia and Africa contribute steadily, 
while the Middle East remains a priority market where 
we intend to strengthen our presence as regional 
conditions stabilize. Alongside deepening our position 
in established overseas markets, we will continue to 
foray into new geographies to expand the growth 
opportunity for our export business.
Our export strategy is based on diversification. 
Capacity can be directed toward domestic institutional 
customers, retail markets or exports based on demand 
and returns. This flexibility reduces dependence on 
any single geography or customer segment. We aim 
to increase export contribution to 20% of sales over 
medium term.
Capacity for the next five years
Capacity addition is central to our five-year plan. 
Sanand Phase I was commissioned in December 
2025 and production at the facility has been ramping 
up steadily month-on-month. We expect Sanand to 
make a major contribution to our topline growth in 
FY 2026-27 as utilization increases throughout the year.
Sanand Phase I adds LT and HT cable capacity and 
includes an electron-beam facility for specialized uses 
in renewables, railways, transportation, aerospace, 
industrial, nuclear plants and other critical infrastructure 
projects. Alongside this, the Chinchpada plant will 
support growth in wires during FY 2026-27, while 
Sanand will drive the increase in cable volumes. 
Sanand Phase II will add EHV cable capacity through a 
vertical tower, along with additional HT cable capacity, 
and is scheduled for commissioning by March 2027. 
This facility is being designed to meet domestic and 
international requirements up to the 500 kV voltage 
grade. It will expand our ability to serve utilities and 
large projects in India and overseas.
During FY 2025-26, we acquired 18 acres of industrial 
land at Salarpur, Rajasthan, close to our existing 
manufacturing facilities. We plan to invest around 
` 700 crore at this location to add cables capacity 
and strengthen backward integration through GI wire 
manufacturing. The new facility is expected to be 
commissioned by September 2028. This facility will 
support business expansion and backward integration. 
We have acquired approximately 70 acres of land in 
Kheda, Vadodara. The conversion of land for industrial 
use is underway and is expected to be completed 
by the end of FY 2026-27, with plant construction 
scheduled to begin the following year.
These investments form a planned capacity pipeline 
for the next few years. We expect annual capital 
expenditure of around ` 600-700 crore, aligned with 
demand across retail, institutional and export markets. 
These investments are intended to support a revenue 
CAGR of around 20% over the medium term.
Technology, quality and market access
Our growth depends on technical capability as much 
as physical capacity. Our NABL-accredited R&D and 
testing infrastructure supports product development, 
customization and qualifications for demanding 
applications. We manufacture EHV cables up to 400 kV 
and are preparing for 500 kV and HVDC applications. 
Our product range includes solutions for renewable 
power, EV infrastructure, marine applications, fire safety 
and specialized industrial use.
Sanand’s vertical tower, electron-beam processing 
capability and export-oriented design will add 
to this base. Global approvals and country-
specific certifications remain essential for utility 
and infrastructure markets. Our experience with 
international testing agencies and major Indian 
authorities reduces the time required to qualify new 
products and enter new accounts.
We are also increasing the use of digital systems 
across manufacturing, quality control, planning and 
performance monitoring. Real-time production visibility, 
digital approvals and better data support faster 
decisions and more consistent execution.

BIODIVERSITY AND ECOSYSTEMS
Healthy ecosystems support resilient communities, reliable 
water systems and long-term economic activity. None of 
our reported plants or offices are located in or around 
ecologically sensitive areas. However, we recognize that 
cable manufacturing and its upstream value chain can 
interact with biodiversity through resource extraction, 
land use, water consumption, emissions, effluents, waste 
and logistics.
Our biodiversity policy applies across manufacturing 
plants, offices and warehouses and extends to employees, 
suppliers and business partners whose activities can 
influence biodiversity outcomes.
We are committed to integrating biodiversity 
considerations into environmental aspects and impact 
assessments under our ISO 14001:2015 framework. Our 
approach follows the mitigation hierarchy, with emphasis on 
avoiding and minimizing impacts on habitats, water bodies 
and species and controlling pollution through responsible 
management of emissions, effluents and waste.
We seek to avoid operations in or near legally protected 
and high-biodiversity-value areas. Responsible sourcing of 
copper, aluminum, PVC and other materials, together with 
recycling and reuse, remains an important part of reducing 
indirect environmental pressure.
Future initiatives being explored include expansion 
of green zones, local conservation programs, wetland 
restoration and community tree planting. We also intend 
to build biodiversity awareness among employees and 
contractors and strengthen engagement with communities, 
regulators and other stakeholders.
Our biodiversity policy aligns with ISO 14001 : 2015, 
the Convention on Biological Diversity and the relevant 
objectives of SDGs 14 and 15.
The next phase will involve progressively mapping site 
proximity to protected areas and Key Biodiversity Areas, 
screening nature-related dependencies and impacts 
across operations and priority raw materials and defining 
measurable, site-specific mitigation actions.
92
KEI Industries Limited

Building Green Manufacturing 
Capacity at Sanand
Case Study 
Our greenfield manufacturing facility at 
Sanand, Gujarat, represents a significant 
step in expanding production capacity while 
embedding environmental considerations 
into infrastructure design and operations. 
Located within the Sanand-II GIDC Industrial 
estate near Ahmedabad, the facility is our 
largest manufacturing plant and is being 
developed in phases to manufacture LT, HT 
and EHV cables. Phase I, focused on LT and HT 
cables, commenced commercial production 
in December 2025, while Phase II, focused 
on EHV cables and HT Cables, is targeted for 
commissioning by March 2027.
Environmental considerations have been integrated into 
the facility’s development approach, with green building 
certification being pursued to support resource-efficient 
infrastructure. The plant is designed to progressively 
incorporate energy-efficient equipment, renewable 
energy, responsible water management, material 
efficiency and robust environmental controls. These 
measures are expected to improve operational 
efficiency and reduce resource and emissions intensity 
as production scales.
The facility will also strengthen our capacity to serve 
infrastructure, renewable energy, power transmission 
and distribution, electric mobility and other specialized 
applications. Its expanded capabilities will support 
growing domestic and international demand while 
enabling us to extend life-cycle thinking, responsible 
material use and efficient manufacturing practices 
across a larger production base.
The Sanand facility reflects our approach to aligning 
capacity expansion with our long-term environmental 
ambitions. By integrating considerations relating to 
energy, water, materials, emissions and waste into the 
facility’s development, we aim to create a scalable 
manufacturing platform that supports business growth 
and operational resilience.

This base gives the wires and cables industry a 
broad demand pool. Renewable generation needs 
evacuation infrastructure. Data centers require 
incoming high-voltage power, medium-voltage 
distribution and copper cables within their facilities. 
Semiconductor and advanced manufacturing plants 
require stable power systems and cables built to exact 
technical standards. Transport and urban projects 
require large quantities of power, signaling, fire-
survival and specialized cables. This is the demand 
behind our investment plan.
Performance review
We closed FY 2025-26 with revenue of ` 11,748 crore, 
an increase of 20.66% over the previous year. EBITDA 
increased by 30.56% to ` 1,388 crore, while EBITDA 
margin improved to 11.81% from 10.92%. Profit after 
tax stood at ` 918 crore, with a PAT margin of 7.82%.
The wires and cables segment grew by 22.32% 
during the year. Higher copper and aluminum prices 
contributed to value growth, while our product mix, 
pricing discipline and operating controls supported 
the improvement in profitability.
Our order book reflects broad-based demand 
across EHV cables, domestic institutional business 
and exports, providing strong visibility across key 
markets and customer segments. This momentum is 
further reinforced by continued growth in our retail 
business, supported by a well-established dealer and 
distribution network and sustained demand across our 
market presence.
Demand across our core markets
Domestic institutional demand remained broad-based. 
Power transmission and distribution, solar and wind 
projects, thermal power generation, oil and gas, 
data centers, railways, metros, highways, tunnels, 
commercial construction and residential development 
continued to generate business. The semi-conductor 
and electronics manufacturing ecosystem is also 
creating demand for stable power infrastructure and 
technically reliable cable solutions.
Domestic institutional cable and wire sales stood at 
` 2,688 crore. Domestic institutional EHV cable sales 
increased by 82% to ` 559 crore. Our existing EHV 
facility operated close to full capacity, supported by 
established approvals, execution experience and 
customer relationships. We expect EHV demand to 
remain strong as India expands transmission capacity 
and strengthens the grid for rising power generation 
and consumption.
The dealer and distribution business delivered sales of 
` 6,349 crore, an increase of 25% and accounted for 
54% of overall sales. Our active dealer base reached 
approximately 2,125 at the end of the year. Housing 
wire sales also grew by approximately 32% during 
the year.
Our retail plan is focused on productivity and market 
quality. We are increasing the network selectively, 
strengthening capable dealers and replacing weaker 
partners where required. Eastern and southern 
India remain priority markets. We are adding sales 
personnel, onboarding dealers and increasing local 
market engagement in these regions. Product quality, 
availability, brand investment and service support will 
remain central to this expansion.
Exponential exports
Export sales increased by 45% to ` 1,833 crore 
during FY 2025-26. We now serve customers across 
more than 60 countries, with established business 
in the Middle East, Australia and Africa and a 
growing presence in Europe and the United States. 
Our export mix includes EHV, HT and LT cables

KEI Industries Limited
Our stainless-steel wire division remained stable 
with annual sales of ` 212 crore and 89% 
capacity utilization. 
As India consolidates its position as a reliable 
manufacturing hub, global demand for LT, HT, and EHV 
cables is gaining momentum – driven by renewable 
energy transitions, urbanization-led infrastructure, and 
the shift to smart grids. This outlook, reinforced by the 
China Plus One strategy, positions KEI to lead across 
domestic and global growth corridors. With retail 
enhancing brand salience, institutional and export 
verticals capturing high-value opportunities, and a 
disciplined EPC footprint, we are scaling with precision 
– ready for the next wave of expansion.
Accelerating innovation and digitization
Innovation remains a key enabler of our growth. 
This year, we strengthened our technology edge 
across both product and process fronts. After over 
three years of development, we began supplying 
Electrical Submersible Pump (ESP) Cables to 
global oilfield markets, becoming the only Indian 
manufacturer in this niche B2B segment. Further, we 
are set to launch high-voltage HVDC cables from our 
Sanand facility, further deepening our presence in the 
extra high voltage domain.
At the Sanand plant, we are also building E-beam 
capacity for cables – used in railway and shipbuilding 
applications – marking another step towards 
completing our product portfolio. Our R&D strategy is 
anchored in domain expertise, supported by overseas 
specialists who drive materials and product innovation.
On the operational front, we advanced our digital 
transformation with machine-level digitization pilots 
at the HT Plant in Bhiwadi. These are designed to 
enhance productivity and reduce downtime. As the 
digital economy expands – with rising demand from 
EVs, data centers, and smart infrastructure – we are 
well-positioned to capture emerging opportunities in 
next-generation cable applications.
Investing ahead of the curve
Our investment philosophy remains simple – anticipate 
demand, stay ahead of constraints, and build capacity 
before it’s needed. FY 2024-25 exemplified this 
approach, as we accelerated capital deployment to 
strengthen our manufacturing footprint and unlock 
scale-driven growth.
We did capital expenditure of ` 698 crore across both 
brownfield expansions and the marquee greenfield 
project in Sanand. The commissioning of expanded 
capacities at Chinchpada and Pathredi enhanced our 
output in key product lines such as house wires and LT 
power cables. With cable division utilization touching 
~85% by year-end, these additions directly supported 
our growth for the year.
Central to our long-term growth agenda is Sanand 
project. The strategically located and technologically 
future-ready facility  will cater to LT, HT, and 
EHV segments – including large-format exports. 
In FY 2024-25 alone, ` 384 crore was invested on 
this project. The first phase will go live by September, 
2025, with full completion targeted by Q1 FY 2026-27. 
Once operational, Sanand will add approx. 
` 5,500-6,000 crore in production capacity. Further to 
secure our long-term visibility, we have acquired 18 
acres land at Salarpur, Rajasthan and in the process of 
acquiring a sizeable land at Kheda, Nadiad, Gujarat.  
Our financial prudence is the core to this scale. 
We have undergone a successful QIP fund raising to 
fund capex, repay debt, and protect internal accruals – 
ensuring we maintain a strong, low-leverage position. 
In FY 2025-26 and 2026-27, we plan to invest another 
` 1,300 crore in Sanand Project. After completion of 
Sanand Project, we endeavor to do capital expenditure 
of ` 700-800 crore each year for the next phase of 
capex for low voltage and medium voltage cables 
which will be funded through internal accruals. 
This long-range view, backed by disciplined execution, 
positions us well to achieve growth in revenue of 
19-20% CAGR over a period of next five years.
Strengthening our foundations responsibly
Sustainability is embedded in the way we design, 
operate, and grow. We strengthen this commitment 
through tangible actions across our environmental 
footprint, workforce development, and community 
engagement. Our approach is guided by long-term 
value creation that balances business performance 
with stakeholder well-being.
We invested in multiple initiatives to reduce our 
environmental impact and drive responsible 
manufacturing. Our plants operate as zero liquid 
discharge facilities, supported by rainwater harvesting 
systems and increased use of renewable energy.

In FY26, we added 9.6 gigawatt of new capacity, and 1.9 gigawatt has already 
been added in FY27 till date. We continue to set benchmarks in operational excellence, 
consistently outperforming the all-India average in both availability factor and plant load factor.  
As can be seen in the slide, our group portfolio stands at around 127 gigawatt, with around 91 
gigawatt as operational and another 36 gigawatt as under-construction assets. Further, with an 
ambitious growth plan, we hope to continue our leadership position. Nearly 41% of the capacity 
would be contributed from our JVs and subsidiaries. 
Turning to our mining business, NTPC group manages an asset base of nine coal mines with a 
combined peak capacity of 92 million metric ton per annum. In FY26, the company achieved a 
production milestone of 48.66 million tons, reflecting a strong operational efficiency in mining. 
And we have now carved it out as a separate company, as you all know, this is the NTPC Mining 
Limited. All the assets, existing assets in NTPC have been transferred. 
Presently, 18% of our coal requirement is met through our captive coal mines, which would go 
up to 25% fulfilment through captive mining by FY30, thus enhancing the fuel security and 
supply reliability. Coming to some of the international ventures, our first international thermal 
project, 2 x 660 MW in Bangladesh, through a 50-50 joint venture with Bangladesh Power 
Development Board, is fully operational since 2024. 
First solar project, 50 megawatt under construction in Sri Lanka through a 50-50 joint venture 
with Electricity Generation Lanka Private Limited. First phase of the project is under 
development, and second phase of 70 megawatt is under planning. Recently, NTPC has 
incorporated a subsidiary company in Mauritius for developing its first floating solar PV project, 
15 megawatt with BESS in Mauritius at Tamarind Falls reservoir. 
NTPC continues to expand its consultancy footprint, securing PMC contracts for 6.6 gigawatt 
of solar projects under the International Solar Alliance and training nearly 560 plus participants 
from 40 countries. These initiatives reinforce our role as a trusted global partner in clean energy 
development and capacity building. 
Now we turn to some of our strategic plans and transition goals. Energy transition is reshaping 
NTPC's future growth trajectory. We are strategically balancing energy security with 
sustainability, ensuring reliable power supply while steadily increasing the share of low-carbon 
and clean energy source in our portfolio. NTPC is steadily transforming into an integrated energy 
major with interests spanning renewables, hydrogen, storage, nuclear, mobility, mining, trading, 
and international business. 
Guided by our new corporate plan, NTPC is charting an ambitious growth trajectory, targeting 
a capacity portfolio of 150 gigawatts by FY32 and on to 250 gigawatts by FY37. This is as per 
our latest business plan. With renewable energy driving a significant share of this expansion, as 
you can see, the share of fossil fuel-based capacity is expected to gradually decline from 82% 
today to 56% by FY32 and further to 39% by 2037. 

 
NTPC Limited 
 
 
July 27, 2026

Much as in absolute terms, the coal capacity will go down, but from point of view of proportion, 
it will shrink. This would be supported by rapid renewable expansion, our entry into nuclear 
energy as well. In billion unit terms, while the overall generation will grow by nearly 7% to 
reach 943 billion units by FY37, the share of renewable energy is expected to increase from the 
current 4.00% to nearly 33% by FY37. 
In the process, the share of fossil-based generation would have declined from 93% to 58%, which 
augurs quite well with our larger national goal of achieving net zero by 2070. As can be seen in 
the slide, our capex projection as per the revised corporate plan is shown in three phases. The 
first phase is the two-year phase, FY26 and '27. 
Group-level capex is INR1,08,000 crores estimates. We have already achieved, incurred 
INR56,000 crores in FY26 out of this. In the second phasing, comprising five years from FY28 
to FY32, total capex would be INR5,97,000 crores, driven primarily by renewable energy 
projects as we move towards our goal of becoming a 60 gigawatt company in the renewable 
space. The third phase will be five years from FY33 to FY37. 
We'll see a major shift towards nuclear power as well, while continuing with the RE project as 
well, with an approximately INR9,63,000 crores as capex. So, the total capex envisaged is 
INR17 lakh crores, as CMD sir was mentioning, over the next 11 years, that is up to financial 
year 37. Renewable energy, of course, would be the key driver of NTPC's future growth, led by

Our renewable portfolio is targeted to reach 60 gigawatts by FY32 and expand further to 136 
gigawatts by FY37. Presently, the operational capacity of RE portfolio stands at 12 gigawatts. 
During FY26, we have added around 4.2 gigawatt, and further, subject to transmission 
infrastructure, we are targeting to add another 7 gigawatts to 8 gigawatts for the renewable

As regards battery energy storage systems, NTPC group has a portfolio of 38.9 gigawatt-hours,

Coming to newer frontiers, steps being undertaken on the nuclear front, we have an ambitious

For sectors that are difficult to electrify directly, such as heavy 
industry and long-distance transport, green hydrogen emerges 
as a key clean-energy carrier. It can serve as a reducing agent in 
green steelmaking, a feedstock for green ammonia and fertilisers, 
a cleaner input for refineries, and the basis for green methanol 
and ammonia in shipping. Under the National Green Hydrogen 
Mission, India aims to produce 5 million tonnes of green hydrogen 
each year by 2030, while NITI Aayog’s Net Zero Scenario projects 
demand rising towards 25 million tonnes by 2050 and around 50 
million tonnes by 2070. Because most green hydrogen is produced 
through renewable-powered electrolysis, its growth is closely linked 
to the expansion of clean power.
The transition is capital-intensive. NITI Aayog estimates cumulative 
investment of around USD 22.7 trillion by 2070 under the Net Zero 
Scenario, with the power sector accounting for over half of the total, 
reflecting its central role in electrifying the wider economy. This 
implies average annual flows of close to USD 500 billion, against 
actual energy investment of about USD 135 billion in 2024 (IEA). 
Mobilising capital on this scale, attracting low-cost finance, and 
building domestic manufacturing and innovation capacity are 
among the defining tasks of the coming decades.
The human dimension of the transition is equally important. NITI 
Aayog’s assessment of the social implications of the transition 
notes that more than 150 districts depend significantly on fossil-
fuel supply chains, and that coal-based power and mining together 
sustain millions of formal and informal livelihoods. Encouragingly, 
the same analysis finds that the Net Zero pathway is expected 
to create more energy-sector jobs than it displaces, with around 
one million additional energy jobs by 2050, alongside substantial 
gains in construction and clean-technology manufacturing, 
provided the transition is managed with care through reskilling, 
livelihood diversification and support for affected communities. 
NTPC remains committed to a just energy transition, ensuring that 
progress towards a cleaner energy system continues to create 
opportunity and shared prosperity.
As the nation’s largest power producer, NTPC has a central role 
to play in this transformation. With an installed and commercial 
group capacity of over 90 GW, NTPC meets close to one-fourth of 
India’s electricity requirement. The Company has built its standing 
on reliability, operational excellence and affordable power, and is 
now applying the same discipline to one of the most ambitious 
diversification journeys in the global power sector. In line with our 
vision to be the world’s leading power company, accelerating India’s 
growth along with energy transition, the company is strengthening 
its existing core business while building a new core in renewables, 
storage, nuclear, green hydrogen and green chemicals.
At the centre of this strategy is The Brighter Plan, NTPC’s roadmap 
to reshape its portfolio around clean energy to address the triple 
bottom line. The Company has set a target of 60 GW of renewable 
energy capacity by 2032, as part of a planned total capacity of 
around 149 GW, with non-fossil sources expected to constitute 
nearly half of the portfolio. This is envisaged to scale up to 244 GW 
by 2037, out of which 136 GW will come from RE portfolio, and the 
non-fossil fuel based capacity will gain 60% of the capacity share. 
To drive this growth, NTPC has carved out and listed NTPC Green 
Energy Limited (NGEL), its dedicated renewable energy arm, which 
has crossed 10 GW of installed capacity and is developing gigawatt-
scale solar, wind and hybrid parks, including the flagship Khavda 
complex in Gujarat, under the Ultra Mega Renewable Energy Power 
Park model. To champion the other part of the clean energy portfolio 
by addition of Nuclear Energy, the company is already in process 
to setup its first nuclear power project in Banswara, Rajasthan 
under its joint venture with Nuclear Power Corporation of India Ltd 
(NPCIL), while setting up another wholly owned subsidiary NTPC 
Parmanu Urja Nigam Limited (NPUNL) to add nuclear capacities 
across India.
Green Hydrogen and the Hard-to-Abate Sectors
Financing the Transition and a Just Energy Transition
NTPC: Powering India’s Energy Transition
A rapidly expanding solar, wind, floating-solar and hybrid 
portfolio, backed by battery storage and pumped-hydro 
projects to firm up variable generation and to provide grid 
balancing and ancillary services.
Pilot and demonstration projects in green hydrogen mobility 
and microgrids, setting up India’s first and largest Green 
Hydrogen Hub at Pudimadaka, Vishakhapatnam, hydrogen 
blending in natural-gas networks, and the production of 
green methanol and green ammonia, alongside carbon-
capture-and-utilization initiatives at our thermal stations.
A foray into nuclear power through ASHVINI, our joint 
venture with NPCIL, advancing projects such as 2.8 
GW Mahi Banswara, in support of a substantial nuclear 
capacity ambition by 2047.
Continued 
investment 
in 
supercritical 
and 
ultra-
supercritical 
technology, 
flue-gas 
desulphurization, 
biomass co-firing and plant flexibilization, and Carbon 
Capture, Utilization and Storage technologies (CCUS) 
pilots, so that the existing fleet can support a renewable-
rich grid while reducing its emission intensity.
Renewables and storage
Green hydrogen and green chemicals
Nuclear
Cleaner, more flexible thermal
Building a Diversified Clean-Energy Portfolio
One conclusion is unmistakable: the power sector is the engine 
of India’s energy transition.

Sharp 
improvement 
in 
performance
Historic Milestones in FY 2025–26
•	
NDC target achievement ahead of schedule: India achieved 
50% non-fossil installed capacity in June 2025, five years 
ahead of its Paris Agreement target, becoming one of the few 
major economies to achieve this milestone.
•	
RE generation record: On 29th July 2025, renewable sources 
met 51.5% of India’s real-time electricity demand of 203 GW, 
the highest-ever intra-day RE share.
•	
Global RE ranking: India became the world’s third-largest 
country by total renewable energy installed capacity (IRENA 
2025), ranking third in solar (150.2 GW), fourth in wind (54.65 
GW).
•	
Record Non-Fossil capacity addition: Non-Fossil capacity 
addition in 2025-26 was 55.29 GW, making it the highest 
capacity addition in a single year for nuclear, large hydro and 
RE combined.
•	
Manufacturing scale-up: Solar Module Manufacturing 
Capacity has increased from 2.3 GW in 2014 to ~172 GW, as 
on 31st March 2026; Wind Turbine Manufacturing Capacity has 
increased from 10 GW in 2014 to ~24 GW, as on 31st March 
2026.
Fuel Mix & Generation
Total electricity generation stood at approximately 1,840 BU in 
FY 2025–26, registering a modest growth of around 1% over FY 
2024–25. Thermal generation declined by about 4%, reflecting the 
increasing penetration of renewable energy, which displaced coal-
based generation, particularly during solar-rich periods.
Renewable electricity generation (including hydro) recorded a 
robust growth of approximately 18%, led by solar (~20% year-on-
year) and wind (~27% year-on-year). Supported by record renewable 
capacity additions and a favourable monsoon that moderated 
cooling demand, coal-based generation declined by around 3.7%, 
marking one of the first notable declines in recent years. Gas-based 
generation also declined significantly by around 18%, while nuclear 
generation witnessed a marginal reduction of approximately 3% 
during the period.
Energy Storage & Grid
Energy storage deployment continued to gain momentum. As per 
the National Generation Adequacy Plan 2026 projections by the 
CEA, India is expected to add ~174 GW / 888 GWh of energy storage 
capacity by 2035, reflecting the growing importance of storage, not 
only for grid balancing but also for integration of rapidly increasing 
variable RE capacity and meet the non-solar hours’ demand.
The national transmission network expanded to approximately 
5 lakh circuit-kilometres, with inter-regional transfer capacity 
increasing to about 120 GW, enhancing grid resilience and 
facilitating renewable integration.
The National Generation Adequacy Plan 2026 has projected India’s 
peak demand to reach ~459 GW and electricity demand to ~3365 
BU by FY 2035–36, underscoring the continued requirement 
for substantial capacity additions across generation and grid 
infrastructure.
Distribution
The Revamped Distribution Sector Scheme (RDSS) continued to 
deliver measurable improvements in the financial and operational 
performance of distribution utilities. The ACS-ARR gap reduced 
significantly from ₹0.78/kWh in FY 2013-14 to ₹0.06/kWh in FY 
2024-25, while AT&C losses reduced from 22.62% in FY 2013-14 
to 15.04% in FY 2024-25, indicating enhanced efficiency and loss 
reduction.
Legacy dues of DISCOMs also witnessed a substantial reduction, 
declining from from ₹1,39,947 crore in 2022 to just ₹3,330 crore 
by March 2026, supported by the implementation of the amended 
Late Payment Surcharge (LPS) Rules.
Under RDSS, smart metering has gained strong traction, with over 
19.79 crore smart meters and 52.53 lakh distribution transformer 
(DT) meters sanctioned, aimed at improving billing efficiency, 
transparency, and demand-side management. 
Key Policy & Regulatory Developments in FY 2025–26
During the year, several regulatory and policy developments were 
introduced to support energy transition, enhance grid flexibility, and 
strengthen market mechanisms:
•	
SHANTI Act, 2025: Landmark legislation replacing the Atomic 
Energy Act 1962 & Civil Liabilities for Nuclear Damage Act, 
2010; permits private Indian companies, foreign companies (up 
to 49% FDI) and joint ventures to build, own and operate nuclear 
plants; paves the way for India’s 100 GW nuclear target by 2047.
•	
Scenarios Towards Viksit Bharat and Net Zero: Sectoral 
Insights: Power by NITI Aayog (Feb 2026): The report 
identifies rapid electrification and large-scale clean energy 
deployment as central to achieving the twin goals of India being 
a USD 30 Trillion economy by 2047 and Net Zero economy 
by 2070; projects electricity to account for nearly 60% of the 
total energy consumption by 2070, with non-fossil sources 
contributing about 98% of power generation; estimates 
cumulative investment requirements of approximately USD 
14.2 trillion in the power sector through 2070 and highlights 
affordable, reliable and low-carbon electricity as a key enabler 
of India’s long-term economic growth and decarbonisation 
pathway.
•	
CERC Tariff Regulations (Second Amendment), 2026: 
Introduced a comprehensive framework for Energy Storage 
Systems (ESS) co-located with thermal plants and ISTS. The 
regulations enable storage for supply to beneficiaries, support 
ancillary services, and enhance renewable energy integration. 
Key provisions include defined norms for battery life (15 years), 
RoE (14%), availability (90%), and efficiency (≥85%). Additional 
provisions include monthly recovery of ash transportation 
costs, incentives for captive coal mining efficiency, and 
introduction of a Regulatory Sandbox to promote innovation.

Energising India’s Growth, 
Powering the Transition
Aligning NTPC’s growth with India’s vision of Viksit Bharat @2047 and Net Zero @2070
India has set itself two defining goals for the decades ahead: to become a developed nation Viksit Bharat by 2047, the centenary of its 
independence, and to achieve Net Zero greenhouse gas emissions by 2070. For NTPC, India’s largest integrated power utility, supporting 
both goals lies at the heart of our purpose and our long-term strategy.
The world's energy system is undergoing a rapid transformation 
as governments and businesses accelerate their decarbonisation 
efforts. According to Net Zero Tracker, 137 countries have 
already established net-zero targets, while 145 countries have 
announced or are considering net-zero commitments. Reflecting 
this global shift, the International Energy Agency (IEA) reports 
that clean energy is attracting an increasingly larger share of 
new investment in power generation worldwide.Solar, wind 
and battery storage are being added to record levels each year, 
supported by a sustained fall in technology costs over the past 
decade. At the same time, governments are placing renewed 
emphasis on energy security, resilient supply chains for critical 
minerals, and the need to keep energy affordable through a 
period of global uncertainty.
India approaches this transition as one of the world’s fastest-
growing major economies and its most populous nation, even as 
its per-capita energy use and emissions remain well below the 
global average. India’s transition is therefore distinctive: it must 
serve a large and rising demand for energy while steadily reducing 
the carbon intensity of that energy. This approach is guided by the 
principles of equity and common but differentiated responsibilities, 
as reflected in India’s commitments under the UNFCCC and its 
Long-Term Low Emission Development Strategy.
The Global Energy Transition
NITI Aayog’s study, Scenarios Towards Viksit Bharat and Net Zero, 
provides a comprehensive assessment of how India can pursue 
rapid development and deep decarbonization together. As per its 
scenarios, India’s economy is projected to grow from around USD 
4.2 trillion in 2025 to about USD 30 trillion by 2047, accompanied by 
rapid urbanization and a multi-fold increase in the output of steel, 
cement and other materials as the country moves closer to global 
per-capita consumption levels.
A notable feature of these scenarios is that energy demand 
grows far more slowly than the economy. Final energy demand is 
projected to rise only about 2.1 to 2.6 times by 2070, even as GDP 
expands roughly elevenfold, on account of greater electrification, 
improved energy efficiency and circularity. Electricity is at the centre 
of this shift. Its share of final energy consumption is projected to 
rise from around 21% at present to as much as 60% by 2070, while 
total electricity demand could grow six to eight times over the 
same period, lifting per-capita consumption towards the levels of 
advanced economies. The pace at which the power grid becomes 
cleaner will, in large measure, determine the pace of decarbonization 
across the wider economy.
Meeting India’s electricity needs cleanly calls for a transformation 
of unprecedented scale. NITI Aayog’s Net Zero Scenario indicates 
that total installed generation capacity could grow roughly fourteen 
times by 2070, with renewable energy forming the new core of 
the grid. Solar becomes the backbone, with capacity potentially 
exceeding 5,000 GW, complemented by more than 1,000 GW of 
wind, including offshore wind off the coasts of Gujarat and Tamil 
Nadu. The share of non-fossil capacity rises from around 40% at 
present to close to 98% by 2070.
India’s Twin Goals: Viksit Bharat and Net Zero
Transforming the Power Sector
As variable renewables come to dominate, energy storage and 
firm power become essential to maintaining reliability. In the 
same scenarios, battery energy storage is projected to scale from 
negligible levels today to 2,500–3,000 GW by 2070, supported 
by 150–165 GW of pumped hydro. Nuclear power emerges as 
a strategic pillar of firm, low-carbon generation, scaling from 
around 8 GW today (Central Electricity Authority) towards 100 GW 
by 2047, in line with the national nuclear mission, and potentially 
300 GW by 2070 in NITI Aayog’s projections, with small modular 
reactors playing an increasing role.
Coal continues to play a vital role through the transition. In the near-
to-medium term, the existing coal fleet remains important for grid 
reliability and for meeting demand during periods of high system 
stress. In these scenarios, coal capacity is expected to peak 
around the mid-2040s before declining as long-duration storage 
and clean alternatives mature. The emphasis, therefore, is on 
improving the efficiency, flexibility and environmental performance 
of the coal fleet so that it can support a renewable-rich grid, while 
avoiding long-term lock-ins. This balanced approach, which 
secures reliability even as the system decarbonises, is precisely 
where a utility of NTPC’s scale and operating experience adds the 
greatest value.
NTPC Koldam

GLOBAL ENERGY & POWER SECTOR LANDSCAPE | FY 2025–26
The year 2025 marked a significant inflection point in the global power sector. For the first time, renewable energy accounted for 33.8% of 
total electricity generation, surpassing coal at 33.0%, signalling a structural shift in the global energy mix. Notably, clean energy sources 
primarily solar and wind met nearly the entire incremental electricity demand, even as the coal-based generation fell (-0.6%) for the first time 
since 2020.
This development underscores a transition that is increasingly driven by economic competitiveness and technological advancement, in 
addition to policy support, indicating that the global energy transition is entering a more self-sustaining phase.

The rapid decline in battery pack costs globally, dropping 45% Y-o-Y 
to nearly $70/kWh in 2025b, is leading to significant reduction in 
levelized cost of storage and hence driving capacity additions, and 
transforming power system dynamics. Storage technologies are

Fuel Security
NTPC has adopted a robust and forward-looking strategy to ensure 
fuel security for its extensive fleet of thermal power plants. This 
strategy focuses on mitigating risks associated with fuel shortages, 
price fluctuations, and logistical challenges by enhancing domestic 
coal production, diversifying procurement sources, and eliminating 
imports. 
The company has secured 100% fuel tie-up for its thermal capacity 
through long-term Fuel Supply Agreements (FSAs) with coal 
companies (CIL & SCCL), with a total Annual Contracted Quantity 
(ACQ) of 256.92 MMT across the NTPC group. During FY 2025–26, 
ACQ materialization from coal companies stood at 84%. NTPC 
further strengthened its fuel security by sourcing 43.5 MMT of coal 
from its captive mines. 
NTPC has also procured domestic coal on FOR (Free on Rail) 
destination basis from commercial mines & surplus coal from 
captive blocks through competitive bidding. Thus, NTPC offset 
the shortfall from linked sources without procuring imported coal, 
thereby reducing the overall cost of power generation.
Captive Coal Mining
To strengthen fuel security, NTPC continues to expand its captive 
coal mining portfolio, with a target to increase production capacity 
from 91.6 MMTPA to 100 MMTPA and beyond.
To enhance operational focus, NTPC has consolidated its mining 
activities under its wholly owned subsidiary, NTPC Mining Limited 
(NML). With the transfer of Pakri Barwadih Coal mine on 01st April 
2026, all the six coal mines have been transferred from NTPC 
to NML. While one mine – Badam- is under development, NML 
currently operates five mines - Pakri-Barwadih, Dulanga, Talaipalli, 
Chatti-Bariatu, and Kerandari, all of which have been declared 
commercial.
Coal production from the captive mines, including production from 
the Amelia mine operated by THDC India Limited, stood at 48.65 
MMT during the year, 6.22% higher than the previous fiscal.
Operations from Badam mine are expected to commence in 
FY 2026–27, while progress continues on the Banhardih mine 
(PVUNL). NML has also secured its first commercial coal block, 
North-Dadhu (Eastern Part) with the mining plan approved, and 
development activities in progress.
In addition to coal, NML is actively pursuing diversification into 
critical minerals, supported by strategic collaborations with leading 
institutions and industry partners.
Through these initiatives, NTPC aims to build a resilient, cost-
effective domestic fuel supply base, while supporting long-term 
energy security and emerging transition requirements.
Power Trading (NVVN)
During FY 2025-26, NTPC strengthened its diversified energy and 
sustainability portfolio through its subsidiary NVVN, delivering 
robust growth across power trading, renewable energy, waste-
to-energy and carbon management businesses. Power trading 
volume increased by 13% to 46.38 BU, driven by strong growth 
in exchange-based and cross-border power trading, including 
addition of the Punatsangchu-II hydro project in Bhutan. The 
Company also expanded its renewable energy portfolio with over 
227 MW of rooftop and ground-mounted solar projects under 
commissioning, construction and tendering stages. Significant 
progress was achieved in waste-to-energy projects at Varanasi, 
Noida, Gorakhpur, Bhopal and Hubballi-Dharwad, while battery 
energy storage projects and consultancy assignments further 
strengthened the clean energy portfolio. During the year, NVVN also 
enhanced its participation in emerging carbon markets, expanded 
gas trading operations, and implemented multiple digital initiatives 
for power exchange bidding, analytics and cross-border scheduling, 
reinforcing its focus on innovation, sustainability and integrated 
energy solutions.
Renewable Energy (NTPC Group)
NTPC continues to expand its capacity in line with India’s growth 
trajectory while advancing its commitment to energy transition and 
net-zero objectives.

Some of the other key developments include business transfer agreement for transfer of coal mines 
from NTPC to NTPC Mining Limited was signed for hiving off coal mining business at an estimated 
value of ₹10,503 crore and Chatti Bariatu and Badam mines have been transferred. We expect to 
complete transfer of all the remaining mines to NML in the current fiscal.  
Receivables from various DISCOMs improved to 28 days from 33 days last year’s same period.  
Honorable Prime Minister of India has laid the foundation stone on 22 September 2025 for two 
hydropower projects of NEEPCO in Arunachal Pradesh. The project includes Heo Hydroelectric 
project (240 MW) and Tato-1 Hydroelectric project (186 MW) having an estimated cost of over 
₹3,700 crore.  
NTPC Vidyut Vyapar Nigam Limited has registered a growth of 11.45% in power trading up from 
22.3 BUs to 24.8 BUs.  
Another important event has been the issuance of CERC Suo Motu order which provides a structured 
framework for scheduling of thermal stations and addresses the issue of supply obligation on 
generator in the event of infeasible schedule by the DISCOMs. It also enables stable plant operations. 
We would be happy to take any further questions on this topic during the Q&A session.  
NGEL secured a contract for supply of 0.7 lakh tonnes of green ammonia in the recently concluded 
green chemical tender, marking its entry into the emerging segment. This win provides opportunity 
to set the foothold in the new market of green hydrogen chemicals under the National Green Hydrogen 
Mission. 
On the nuclear side, Honorable Prime Minister laid the foundation stone of Mahi Banswara Rajasthan 
Atomic Power Project (4 x 700 MW) in Banswara, Rajasthan on 25 September 2025. The Government 
of India has approved the transfer of the project from NPCIL to ASHVINI at book value and 
excavation work is expected to commence shortly.  
While we expand into new areas, we remain steadfast on our prudent practices and core strengths. 
We are expediting new capacities in coal, renewable and nuclear. Additionally, we are exploring 
opportunities in energy storage, green chemicals and other new technology areas including our 
international presence.  

NTPC Limited 
  October 30, 2025 
 
 
 
 
 
 
Page 8 of 18 
 
As highlighted during annual investor meet, we have revised our capacity addition target from 
existing 130 GW to 149 GW by 2032 and 244 GW by 2037. Accordingly, the estimated capital 
expenditure requirement is 7 lakh crore by 2032. Our current capacity under construction stands at 33 
GW consisting of 17 GW coal, 2 GW hydro and 14 GW renewable. 
 
To achieve the targeted capacity addition Plan, we are well on track to place awards of contracts of 
new capacities in both coal and renewable. In the current fiscal, pending some minor clearances, we 
have placed Limited Notice To Proceed order for 2400 MW Meja II expansion to be executed through 
Meja Urja Nigam (P) Limited (MUNPL), JV with Uttar Pradesh. We have also placed fresh contracts 
for 3 GW of renewable capacity. Additionally, contract for land and connectivity was placed for 1200 
MW.  
We are also systematically looking out for large parcels of land banks for our solar projects as 
connectivity becomes automatically available for large capacity projects with huge land banks.  
Allotment of land parcels by various state governments with aggregate capacity of 16.5 GW is in 
advanced stage (4 GW Andhra Pradesh, 10 GW Rajasthan, 2.5 GW Gujarat, 6.5 GW through tenders). 
With this, our total land pool has reached 22.8 GW.  
We are exploring partnerships with various international players in the nuclear domain to prepare 
ourselves for setting up capacities in our nuclear subsidiary NTPC Parmanu Urja Nigam Limited once 
we get required permissions from the government. 
 
Way Forward 
FY26 so far has been a strong year for both NTPC and NGEL with record capacity addition and 
healthy financial performance. A major milestone has been the foundation stone laying of the Mahi 
Banswara project which marks formal beginning of NTPC's nuclear energy journey.  
As we look ahead to the second half of FY26, we remain optimistic about both the economy and the 
power sector.  
 
For NTPC, the focus remains on the timely completion of under construction projects, strengthening 
fuel security and continuously improving plant efficiency and availability.  
India is once again adding substantial thermal capacity. We are a key part of this national mission. At 
the same time, NGEL is driving expeditious execution of renewable projects to ensure capacity ramp 
up, supporting our goal of achieving 60 GW of RE capacity by FY32.  
We are also exploring opportunities in battery storage and hybrid projects to deliver renewable power 
round the clock and strengthen our clean energy portfolio.  

NTPC Limited

The nation is progressing towards becoming a developed economy, in turn increasing the power 
demand. As a key player in the power sector, we are ensuring that we meet this demand while staying 
ahead of the competition.  
We are committed to enhancing shareholders' wealth and continue to strive for improving 
performance in every facet of our business. Thank you for joining us.

Beginning with Indian economy and the structural outlook, India continues to be the fastest-
growing major economy, with IMF projecting GDP growth of 6.4% in 2026, well above all G7 
nations and key BRICS member countries. Now, despite global uncertainties, Indian economy's 
fundamentals remain strong, supported by robust domestic demand, infrastructure investment, 
and policy reforms. The economy also outperformed expectations in 2025 calendar, recording 
7.7% growth against the IMF estimates of 6.2%. 
For the power sector, this growth story is highly significant. Large-scale industrialization, rapid 
urbanization, technology-led digitalization, and widespread electrifications are expected to drive 
sustained growth in electricity demand for decades to come. This provides a strong foundation 
for NTPC's consistent and enduring growth as we continue to support India's development 
journey while creating long-term value for our stakeholders. 
Recently, NITI Aayog released guiding report on Viksit Bharat, the Developed India, and net 
zero, projecting that India is poised to become a developed country by 2047 with GDP of USD30 
trillion. This transformation is expected to be driven by a sustained 9% CAGR supported by 
India's favourable demographic profile, abundant renewable energy potential, and continued 
investment in infrastructure and industrial development. 

 
NTPC Limited 
 
 
July 27, 2026 
 
Page 7 of 24 
 
India has set an ambitious target of achieving net zero emission by 2070, driven by a significant 
expansion of renewable energy, strategic deployment of nuclear power, and large-scale adoption 
of energy storage technologies. The non-fossil fuel share, as you can see, would be 90% in the 
year 2050 from the current 53%. In generation terms, share of non-fossil sources would be 78% 
by 2050 from 29% as of FY26. 
Going further, by 2070, non-fossil sources are expected to account for nearly 98% of installed 
capacity. That's when we achieve the net zero and deliver 100% electricity generation. 
Achieving this vision will require cumulative investment of a whopping USD22.7 trillion, of 
which the power sector alone is expected to account for over USD12.3 trillion, underscoring its 
pivotal role in the India's decarbonisation journey. 
As at 30th June 2026, India's total installed power capacity has grown to over 549 gigawatt, with 
297 gigawatt of non-fossil fuel capacity, highlighting the significant progress being made in the 
nation's energy transition journey. Solar power continues to lead this transformation, driving 
renewable capacity growth and reinforcing India's position among the world's leading clean 
energy markets. India further achieved the milestone of 50% cumulative installed capacity from 
non-fossil fuel source in June 2025, five years ahead of its target set by its Nationally Determined 
Contribution to Paris Agreement commitment. 
India's electricity requirement is projected to grow from 1,708 billion units in FY26 to 8,100 
billion units by FY50 and further to 13,000 billion units by FY70. These are all the NITI Aayog 
figures. Correspondingly, peak demand is expected to rise from 245 gigawatt in FY26 to 750 
gigawatt by FY50 and further on to 1,200 gigawatt by FY70, with demand already touching a 
record 271 gigawatt in May 2026. 
As per NITI Aayog, per capita electricity consumption is expected to nearly grow by a CAGR 
of 6% to 6,400 units by 2050 and further to 10,000 units by 2070, aligning it to the then global 
average. These strong fundamentals underpin the power sector potential for sustained growth, 
positioning it as a compelling avenue for long-term value creation for the investors. 
With this favourable sectoral outlook, let me now discuss NTPC's plans and its roadmap for 
long-term and growth and value creation. As the nation's largest power producer, NTPC 
continues to serve as the backbone of India's energy infrastructure, economic growth, and 
prosperity. Our vision is to emerge as the leading player in the global energy landscape. This 
vision is anchored in our unwavering commitment to NTPC group's core values, which you are 
able to see here. 
We call it acronym ICOMIT. It is Integrity, Customer-centric approach and agility, 
Organizational pride, Mutual trust and respect, Innovation and learning, and a clear focus on 
Total quality and safety. NTPC group currently operates over 90 gigawatt of commercial 
capacity, while another 35.7 gigawatt is under construction, underscoring the scale of its growth 
ambitions. Our share, as CMD sir was saying, in the country's electricity generation is 24% with 
just 17% of installed capacity. 

 
NTPC Limited 
 
 
July 27, 2026 
 
Page 8 of 24 
 
Even at this huge scale, we have been continuously demonstrating exceptional all-round 
performance.

Vijay Nirani:  
So globally there is already a mandate sir and airline carriers like Qantas, Norwegian Airlines, 
to an extent Lufthansa, United Airways in America, all these have already made public 
announcements for consuming. If you look at the domestic also, recently Air India and Indian 
Oil have also made an announcement for long term use of SAF into the ATF mix. So globally 
there is consumption that has already started since 2025 onwards. 
Now just to give you clarity sir, CORSIA, that is the body that regulates carbon emissions, has 
given mandates on a voluntary basis from 2024 onwards. And on a mandate basis from 2027 
onwards. So 2027 that is next year onwards globally there is -- it is going to be a compulsory 
blending. 
But a few countries European Union is actually putting taxes, the carbon taxes for promoting 
use of SAF. Whereas certain countries -- India is still deriving its policy as to how that 
promotion has to happen. So, we are waiting for the Indian policy framework as to how they 
will actually promote the consumption.

chunks.body:
Atul Daga: 
Thank you so much, Michelle and good evening, and a very warm welcome to all of you for this 
earnings call for Quarter 4, FY '25 for UltraTech. It's a maze of numbers, which we'll try and 
help you decipher. 
 
I believe the world is redefining its ways of working. The uncertainties around the U.S. tariffs 
are making people wonder what to do next. I believe investors and industry captains globally 
must be revisiting their business strategies. But we, in cement in India, continue our work with 
a renewed focus on the growth opportunities that are unfolding in the country. 
 
To give you a heads up, this year cement industry has ended with a capacity of about 655 million 
tons, up from 625 million tons. And at UltraTech, out of this 30 million tons of new capacity 
addition, almost 57% has been added by UltraTech. However, our overall capacity share in the 
country has gone up from 140 million tons to 184 million tons, an addition of 42.6 million tons 
under our fold with the 2 new acquisitions that we had done. 
 
We believe that this quarter, cement demand overall for the country would have grown around 
4%. And in that backdrop, UltraTech has done close to 10% volume growth. Last quarter of 
fiscal '25 was very eventful for us at UltraTech. After a tedious long-drawn process, we 
successfully completed the transfer and registration of mines in Telangana and Karnataka for 
the cement units that we acquired from Kesoram. 
 
With effect from 1st of March 2025, we have fully taken charge of these units. After obtaining 
an unconditional CCI approval, we had started working with these units earlier on, helping them 
improve their performance. Happy to inform that our efforts have been reflected in their 
performance in the first month of operating control that we took charge. 
 
We started operating these assets from the 1st of March '25, though as per NCLT approval, the 
financial performance of Kesoram with effect from 1/4/24 has to be consolidated with the 
financials of UltraTech. As a result, in the quarter ended March '25, whilst effectively we were 

      
UltraTech Cement Limited 
 
 
April 28, 2025 
 
Page 3 of 17 
 
managing the operations from 1st March '25, the results for the quarter are a mix of performance 
by old management and the new management. 
 
India Cements, we took over the company from the Christmas of December '24. I'm delighted 
to inform you that the company has achieved an EBITDA breakeven in the first quarter after the 
takeover. Second case of sweet success was sales of more than 1 million metric tons in the month 
of March by India Cements. 
 
With prices improving in the South markets from April, this will only reflect in further 
improvement in the company's performance. During this year, we target to cross an EBITDA 
per metric ton of INR500. FY '27 should be crossing INR800 and thereafter, a 4-digit mark. The 
team has chalked out a capex plan of about INR1,500 crores for India Cements, out of which 
INR1,000 crores is towards WHRS and other profit improvement opportunities with a payback 
period of less than 3 years. This will be spent in fiscal '26 and '27 and the benefits will start 
reflecting in the performance of the company in the quarter of Jan, March '27. 
 
We have also identified brownfield expansion opportunities in the network of India Cements for 
future. At UltraTech, we never have a dull moment. We grabbed a small opportunity to 
strengthen our position in the white cement business with the acquisition of cement putty 
manufacturing facility. This is a small transaction, which should get concluded in the next few 
days. 
 
Good things have a cost. Yes, we have leveraged our balance sheet, but are not alarmed at all 
with the current position. Net debt-to-EBITDA is what we ended with 1.16x at the end of March 
'25. With the sales volumes continuously increasing, performance of the company continuously

In April 2026, an additional 8.7 MTPA 
was commissioned. As a result, UltraTech’s total domestic grey cement manufacturing capacity has crossed the 200 MTPA 
milestone, standing at 200.1 MTPA. Including its international footprint of 5.4 MTPA, UltraTech’s global cement manufacturing 
capacity now stands at 205.5 MTPA, firmly entrenching the company’s position as the largest cement producer outside China. 
The company plans to add ~37 million tonnes of capacity, which is expected to take the total installed capacity to over 242.5 
million tonnes by FY28-end. The company successfully completed the migration of the acquired India Cements Limited and 
Kesoram cement businesses to the UltraTech brand by March 2026 end. Successful completion of the brand integration is expected 
to enhance market positioning, strengthen brand recall, and support the realisation of operational and commercial synergies from 
acquisitions. 
 
In FY26, the company exhibited strong revenue growth, with topline increasing by ~16.53% to ₹88,511.53 crore (PY: ₹75,955.13 
crore). Improvement was primarily driven by higher sales volumes and modestly better realisations. Volumes grew by ~13.56% 
to 154.25 MT (PY: 135.83 MT), while blended realisations improved by ~2.68% to reach ₹5665 per tonne in FY26. Robust revenue 
performance, and a higher share of green power and benefits from operating leverage, led to a notable improvement in 
profitability. PBILDT increased to ₹17,020 crore (PY: ₹12,557 crore), with margins expanding to ~19.23% (PY: 16.53%). In 
Q1FY27, the company reported a 15.5% y-o-y growth in total operating income (TOI) to reach ₹24,778 crore, primarily driven 
by higher sales volumes, which grew by ~12.2% y-o-y. Despite rise in raw material costs and increased packaging costs in the 
quarter, PBILDT margins remained stable at 20.35% in Q1FY27 against 20.73% in Q1FY26. 
 
Regionally diversified revenue streams supported by pan-India installed capacities 
Being a commoditised product, cement is significantly cost sensitive and freight/transportation cost is among major costs. Plant 
location usually dictates the company’s major target geographies. UltraTech has 34 integrated manufacturing units, 36 grinding 
units, one clinkerisation unit, and 10 bulk packaging terminals. The company has a presence across regions, with the highest 
capacity in south India at 50.5 MTPA, followed by north India (37.5 MTPA), west India (34.5 MTPA), east India (33.3 MTPA), and 
central India (35.6 MTPA), and overseas (5.4 MTPA) as on March 31, 2026. UltraTech has a network of over 1.45 lakh channel 
partners across the country and has a market reach of over 80% across India. In the white cement segment, UltraTech goes to 
market under the brand name of Birla White. It has two white cement units and four wall care putty units, with a current capacity 
of 3.3 MTPA. With 465 ready mix concrete (RMC) plants in 167 cities, UltraTech is the largest manufacturer of concrete in India.  
 
Sound operating efficiencies supported by integrated operations 
The company’s large scale of operations is supported by its internal operating efficiencies, allowing it to control costs and have a 
wide market reach. The company has established captive thermal powerplant (TPP) of 1,333 MW, WHRS of 414 MW, and 
renewable energy (solar and wind energy) of 1.39 GW as on March 31, 2026, making it self-sufficient for a significant portion of 
its power requirements being cost effective. The company also benefitted from increasing its low-cost green power mix to 43% 

3 
CARE Ratings Ltd. 
 
Press Release  
in FY26. It is targeting to increase green power mix to 85% by 2030. The company also has captive limestone reserves to fully 
meet its requirements for the long term. The company also has split geographical units (GUs) for accessing wider market. This 
has helped the company maintain healthy operating margins in the range of 21-26% for three fiscal years ending FY22, though 
moderation was observed in FY23 to 15.97%, considering significant cost inflation particularly in power and fuels costs. In FY24 
and FY25, prices of pet coke and coal moderated leading to power and fuel cost reducing from ₹1,749 per tonne in FY23 to 
₹1,536 per tonne in FY24 and ₹1,356 per tonne in FY25.  
 
In FY26, fuel cost further moderated to ₹1270 per tonne, owing to increase in green power mix. This and other efficiencies and 
slight improvement in blended realisations resulted into PBILDT/tonne improving from ₹924 per tonne to ₹1103 per tonne. 
However, due to the ongoing West Asia crisis fuel cost is expected to rise with price of pet coke reaching to ~$150-160/tonne. 
However, the company has long-term fuel contracts, which shall help to partially mitigate the risk arising from increase in fuel 
prices. 
 
Robust capital structure and strong debt coverage indicators 
The company’s credit profile is supported by a sustained strengthening in its capital base, with net worth improving to ~₹62,917 
crore as of March 31, 2026, from ₹56,180 crore as of March 31, 2025. This growth reflects healthy internal accruals driven by 
strong operating performance, even after accounting for the payout of a one-time special dividend of ₹240 per share. Continuous 
accretion to reserves, backed by the company’s established scale of operations and above-average operating margins, underscores 
its strong earnings retention capacity and provides a buffer to absorb potential business risks.
