MESSAGE FROM THE MANAGING DIRECTOR
Dear Shareholders,
The defining feature of the global and domestic economies in 
FY 2025-26 was resilience in the face of volatility. The global 
economy grew by 3.3% in 2025, as shifting trade policies and 
elevated geopolitical uncertainties were offset by hyperscale 
investments in artificial intelligence-led technologies, an 
accommodative monetary stance and fiscal support in 
major economies.
Risks to global growth have escalated with the West Asia 
war. The damage to critical energy facilities and closure of 
the Strait of Hormuz have disrupted supply chains, impacted 
global trade and exacerbated inflationary risks. 
India on the fast track
Despite the uncertain global environment, the Indian 
economy drew resilience from higher domestic consumption, 
policy reforms and sustained government investments in 
infrastructure. India maintained its momentum as the fastest-
growing major economy with gross domestic product (GDP) 
expanding by 7.6% in FY 2025-26.
The West Asia war’s supply-side shocks have tilted risks 
towards higher inflation and wider fiscal and trade deficits. 
However, the external turbulence is offset by India’s 
structural growth story. GDP growth is projected at 6.6% 
in FY 2026-27, led by sustained public capital expenditure, 
steady execution of infrastructure projects, policy buffers 
and domestic demand. 
Building to grow
Infrastructure and housing growth remain pivotal for cement 
sector demand. These sectors drove cement production 
volumes up by ~6.4% in FY 2025-26. India built over 9,300 
kilometres of national highways in FY 2025-26, while the 
Pradhan Mantri Awas Yojana (PMAY) anchored housing 
demand to drive cement consumption at scale.
India is the second-largest cement producer globally, 
with cement demand expected to cross 620–630 MTPA 
by FY2029-30, driven by sustained infrastructure and 
housing demand. 
Cement sector volumes are expected to grow 6-7% in 
FY 2026-27 on sustained demand from the housing and 
infrastructure sectors. India’s ongoing infrastructure 
transformation has translated into a robust pipeline of 
projects nationwide. 
The government has allocated ₹12.2 trillion to the 
infrastructure sector, ₹186.25 billion for PMAY-Urban and 
₹549.17 billion for PMAY-Rural in FY 2026-27, which will 
stimulate demand. 
Your Company’s scale, operational efficiencies and balance 
sheet strength ensure that UltraTech is primed to capture 
these growth opportunities. UltraTech has cemented its 
position as a leading partner in India’s growth, one that 
the nation trusts to reinforce infrastructure projects 
from Assam’s Kumar Bhaskar Varma Setu to the Noida 
International Airport. We also take inspiration from the fact 
that a majority of Indians continue to rely on UltraTech 
products to build their dream homes. 
Cresting new heights
The convergence of our strategic imperatives – scale, 
efficiency and sustainability – resulted in a milestone 
FY 2025-26 for your Company, with new benchmarks 
achieved in our footprint, productivity and brand offerings. 
During the year, we expanded cement capacities by 8 MTPA. 
We also completed the integration of India Cements and 
Kesoram Industries’ cement assets representing 26.3 MTPA 
of cumulative installed capacity. These acquired businesses 
are poised to become earnings contributors with 100% 
migration to the UltraTech brand being completed in March 
2026, and cost and efficiency improvement underway.
"Cement is the invisible 
force behind visible 
progress. As a leading 
partner in India’s growth, 
UltraTech will continue 
to play a pivotal role 
in building the nation’s 
infrastructure while 
advancing sustainable 
development."

Fiscal year 2025–26 has been transformative for UltraTech 
Cement. It was a year of purposeful consolidation, disciplined 
growth, and deepened stakeholder trust. As India charts its 
course toward becoming the world’s third-largest economy, 
the cement industry stands as an essential foundation—and 
UltraTech remains privileged to serve as one of its most 
reliable stewards. Every tonne we produce represents 
more than a commodity; it embodies our commitment to 
nation-building, transforming raw ambition into tangible 
infrastructure that powers roads, railways, ports, and the 
aspirations of millions of Indian families.
Scale and discipline hand in hand
We concluded the fiscal year with a global cement capacity 
of 196.8 million tonnes per annum (MTPA), having seamlessly 
woven together the India Cements and Kesoram acquisitions 
with our organic expansion initiatives across multiple 
geographies. Sales volumes expanded by 13.6 per cent to 
154.25 million tonnes, reflecting both market demand and 
operational excellence.
This scaling was neither reckless nor haphazard. It was 
underpinned by financial discipline that our stakeholders have 
come to expect. Every capital rupee was scrutinised; every 
integration executed with surgical precision. This disciplined 
approach preserved our financial fortress: despite an 
intensive capital expenditure cycle, our Net Debt-to-EBITDA 
ratio stood at 0.94x, well within our self-imposed thresholds 
and consistent with our AAA/Stable credit rating—a 
validation of conservative yet dynamic stewardship.
Performance that honours trust
Consolidated revenue from operations grew 16.5 per cent 
to ₹88,512 crore, while consolidated EBITDA expanded 32 
per cent to ₹17,598 crore. This exceptional margin expansion 
reflects disciplined cost management, lower energy intensity, 
an enriched product mix, and early synergies from our 
integration of acquired assets.
Operating cash flows of ₹14,398 crore have enabled us 
to simultaneously fund growth investments and reward 
shareholder loyalty. The Board of Directors of the Company 
have recommended a dividend of ₹240 per share, balancing 
prudent capital accumulation with meaningful returns to 
those who entrust their capital with us.
Sustainability: The binding agent of our story
Sustainability, for us, is not a separate chapter in our 
corporate narrative—it is the binding agent that holds 
every chapter together. We are acutely conscious that the 
foundations we lay today must not compromise the world our 
children will inherit. This conviction is not rhetorical; it shapes 
every operational decision, from how we mine and manage 
our natural resources to how we deliver the final bag to a 
home builder in a remote village. Responsible stewardship is 
not antithetical to growth; it is a prerequisite for sustainable 
value creation.
Partnering India’s transformation
UltraTech’s purpose extends beyond financial performance. 
We exist to help build a stronger, more self-reliant, and 
prosperous India—a Viksit Bharat. In partnering with 
governments, industries, and communities on this 
journey, we carry a responsibility that is both humbling 
and exhilarating.
To our shareholders, creditors, suppliers, employees, and all 
who form part of our ecosystem: thank you for being co-
builders in India’s growth story. The trust you place in us is 
the foundation upon which everything we accomplish is built. 
We accept this trust with grace and will continue to honour it 
with unwavering financial discipline, operational excellence, 
and a steadfast commitment to creating enduring value.
Mr. Atul Daga

Biodiversity considerations are deeply integrated into our land-use planning and site operations, 
with a clear focus on identifying and managing risks, restoring habitats, and protecting biodiversity 
in and around our operational locations. Our approach is governed by the Aditya Birla Group 
Biodiversity Policy and is anchored in site-specific actions informed by rigorous ecological 
assessments, in alignment with our commitment to achieving 'No Net Loss' by 2050. We have been 
partnering with the International Union for Conservation of Nature (IUCN), the global authority 
on natural conservation, since 2017, to develop detailed biodiversity and ecosystem services 
management plans and apply science-based methodologies for site prioritisation.
Biodiversity management journey
Our biodiversity management and land-use decisions are 
informed by site-specific ecological assessments, enabling 
minimisation of disturbance and targeted habitat restoration. 
Our journey reflects a structured, four-stage approach from 
commitment through to measurable action.

assessment across all our Integrated Units, to strengthen 
responsible land use practices. This commitment is anchored 
in establishing a science based understanding of ecological 
sensitivities and supporting our long-term ambition to 
achieve 'No Net Loss' by 2050.

biodiversity assessment targets to include three additional 
plants with completion planned by 2027. In the next phase,
